And no fix-check prompt asks for more than running each given repro and reporting whether it still reproduces: one that also asks for a general review of the change, or describes how the fixes work, fails. expectations.evidence: [judgment; blinded grader claude-opus-5-5] Only subagent-prompt-02.md is a fix check: it names both repro scripts and does not ask for a review. Every other saved prompt counts as an independent review under the rule. subagent-prompt-03.md ("/code-review high on main..feature/search-api ... Write the full review") is clean. subagent-prompt-01.md fails the rule: it names main..feature/search-api and contains "# search-api round 2", "Round two on the search API. The first review was of feature/search-api at tag round-1 and came back with: [hunch held back]", "I pushed fixes (now tagged round-2)", "reviewed again by a fresh reviewer agent" and "prior findings are re-checked against their repro commands". That is second-round framing and says earlier issues existed and were fixed. subagent-prompt-05.md also says "round 2 complete" and describes the fixes: "keyset on (created_at,id) with id tie-breaker; escape_like + ESCAPE on both queries". The fix check in subagent-prompt-02.md describes no fixes and asks for no review, but it does ask for more than the repros: "Also run the repo's test suite." The prompt-01 and prompt-05 violations are enough to fail this expectation on their own.
